name: Intact Raptor Horn
summary: Across the Barrens, hunters seek whole raptor horns. Mebok Mizzyrix of Ratchet hopes to make tonics from them, trusting rumors that these raptors are clever.

sections.title: A Questionable Ingredient
sections.body: Hunters prize raptor hides, talons, and trophies, yet whole horns are harder to take in the field. Mebok Mizzyrix is an eccentric goblin alchemist in Ratchet. He believes Barrens raptors are more cunning than their kin elsewhere, and suspects their intellect lies in their horns. So he hopes to grind whole horns into tonics and bottle that supposed genius in drinks for sale.

sections.title: Stalking the Prides
sections.body: A horn fit for brewing must come from a particularly vicious predator, not just any young raptor. Sunscale Scytheclaws prowl the southern plains and the northern borders near Ashenvale. Takk the Leaper and the elusive Ishamuhale are notable terrors of the veldt. Their stout horns can survive the clash of the hunt intact.

faq.q: Who wants these intact raptor horns?
faq.answer: Mebok Mizzyrix, a goblin merchant and aspiring brewer in Ratchet, seeks intact horns. He believes they hold the key to his next scheme for making money.

faq.q: Why do the horns need to be intact?
faq.answer: Mebok plans to grind whole horns into a fine powder for people to swallow. Hunters discard chipped or broken horns, or consider them spent, because they lack the full potency he hopes to harness in his recipes.
Mature Sunscale Scytheclaws carry them in the northern and southern extremes of the Barrens. Notorious raptors, including Ishamuhale and Takk the Leaper, bear them too.

faq.q: Do raptor horns actually make you smarter?
faq.answer: Barrens raptors show unusual pack cunning and coordination. No one has proved that their intelligence rests in their horns or can pass to someone through a drink.

angles.text: As a hunter, taking a trophy horn whole calls for a clean kill against some of the savannas' fiercest predators.
As a cook, you may hear Mebok plans to pulverize the horns for wine infusions. Practical survivors favor raptor parts for making tools over palatable food.
